chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

No believer would escape from one of three, and perhaps all three would be gathered upon him – either the hatred of the one who happens to be with him in the house, closing the door upon him, bothering him; or a neighbour who would bother him; or the one in his way to his needs who would trouble him.

And if a believer were to be at the top of a mountain, Allah Mighty and Majestic would Send a devil (shaytan) to him who would harm him, and Allah would Make his iman (faith) to be a comfort (uns) for him, such that he would not yearn for anyone with it.

key_terms.أُنْساً: comfort/intimacy (uns) – the deep spiritual solace and companionship that iman provides, displacing the need for any human company
key_terms.إِيمَانِهِ: his iman (faith) – the believer's own faith, which becomes his inexhaustible inner refuge against loneliness and harm
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنُ: the believer – the person of iman who is the unavoidable subject of these three trials
key_terms.بُغْضُ: hatred/enmity – the hostile disposition of a housemate who shuts his door on the believer and causes him harm
key_terms.جَارٌ: neighbour – the second of the three guaranteed sources of tribulation for the believer
key_terms.حَوَائِجِهِ: his needs/errands – the daily affairs and pursuits during which a third party may obstruct or harm the believer
key_terms.شَيْطَاناً: a devil (shaytan) – an agent of harm decreed by Allah even for the utterly isolated believer, affirming that tribulation is inescapable
key_terms.قُلَّةِ: summit/peak – the topmost point of a mountain, used to convey absolute isolation from all human society

ai.seo_question: What three inevitable trials does every believer face according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Imam Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) declares that every believer is inevitably tested by at least one of three social trials: harm from a housemate, a troublesome neighbour, or someone who obstructs him while he is attending to his needs. He then emphasises that even complete isolation offers no escape, as Allah would dispatch a devil to afflict the believer wherever he may be – yet in compensation, Allah makes the believer's iman itself a source of inner comfort (uns), rendering him spiritually self-sufficient and at peace without need of anyone else.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from usman Bin Isa, from Ibn Muskan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

having said: ‘No Momin would escape from one of the three, and perhaps all three would be gathered upon him – either the hatred of the one who happens to be with him in the house, closing the door upon him, bothering him; or a neighbour who would bother him; or the one in his way to his needs, would trouble him.

And if a Momin were to be at the top of a mountain, Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic would Send a Satanla to him who would harm him, and Allahazwj would Make his Emān to be a comfort for him, he would not yearn for anyone with it’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from ibn Muskan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

A believer cannot escape one of three problems or perhaps all three at the same time: someone at home always bites him and closes his door to hurt him, a neighbor who annoys him, or someone on his way to work troubles him.

Even if a believer may live on top of a mountain, Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, sends Satan, who hurts him, but He makes his belief a source of comfort, and with it he does not feel frightened from anyone.”
